lines.text: Same app. One word makes it start sixteen times faster.
Why? Every import runs before your code even starts.
And pandas isn't one file. It's five hundred and sixty-five.
Just to show help, it loads eight hundred and ninety-two modules… and uses none.
Coders used to hide imports inside functions to dodge this.
Python 3.15 makes it one word: lazy.
lines.say: Python three fifteen makes it one word: lazy.

lines.text: Now each import is a token, like at a dosa counter. It loads only when it's used. Never used? Never loaded.
Why so late? Making all imports lazy was rejected in 2022: too risky. So now it's opt-in, line by line.
Faster startup, less memory, cleaner code. The catch: a broken import fails when it's used, not at startup.

notes: hold = minimum seconds from this line's start to the next line's start (the beat length). Lines that run long stretch their beat. `say` is what the TTS speaks when it differs from the on-screen wording. kokoro_voice/kokoro_speed are for the offline voice (scripts/gen/kokoro_tts.py); speed is for HeyGen.
